The two specific asks

Already tracked · #819 jmiedreich-ux/Vennusign#819

1. "View all" — yes, it's still broken on a menu with real history

Opened "QA timing c29341" (real history: a rename, two item adds, a section add, a publish, and a reorder) and clicked View all. Exactly what you suspected: on a menu with enough real activity, the dialog's own entry list has no height cap, so it grows to fit every entry and the modal extends past the viewport — no scroll, title and Close button both pushed out of frame.

This was already found and filed by you as #819 before this run (root cause: the dialog reuses the sidebar panel's .builder__page-history-list, whose overflow-y: auto only works inside the sidebar's grid-constrained track — inside a plain position: fixed dialog it has nothing to overflow against). A fix is already written and on PR #821, not yet merged. I independently reproduced it tonight on the live deployed build and added a confirming comment to #819 with fresh numbers rather than filing a duplicate.

Repro (independent, tonight)
  • Menu "QA boardfit 883b6b" (16 real history entries), viewport 1600×700.
  • view-all-dialog bounding box: {x: 580, y: -49.5, width: 440, height: 799} against a 700px-tall viewport.
  • At 1600×900 the dialog is already 799px tall against a 900px viewport — right at the edge; it scales directly with entry count.

Once entry count is low enough to fit, the dialog renders correctly and reads clearly — see the working example under Findings below, from before it overflows.

Owner's honest read requested

2. Price-less-item publish confirmation — placement is fine; here's my honest read

Created a price-less item, added it to a fresh board, and clicked Publish. My honest read: I don't see a placement problem. It's a small, centered modal — dead-center of the viewport by measurement, not just by eye — using the exact same .builder__dialog/.builder__scrim mechanism as every other confirmation in the builder (discard draft, delete section, review). Tested with 1 item and with 3 (including a deliberately very long name) at both 1600px and 1024px desktop widths: it wraps and scrolls cleanly, both buttons stay reachable, nothing overlaps the canvas or the inspector oddly.

If there's real unease about it, I don't think it's the placement — it's that visually the dialog carries the same light weight as a routine "discard draft?" prompt, for something that's about to put a $0 price in front of a paying customer's guest. That's a legitimate design opinion worth weighing (bigger, a warning color, a different icon), but it isn't a bug, and I'd rather say that plainly than manufacture a placement finding that isn't there.

Findings2 new, filed tonight

Moderate jmiedreich-ux/Vennusign#823

"Go back to…" briefly insists a just-published menu was never published

Found while chasing the "View all" ask above — its sibling dialog, from the same #799/#812 work, has a real gap of its own. "Go back to…" has no loading state. While its own history fetch is still in flight, it renders the same empty-list check as if the fetch had already finished and come back empty, so for the first few seconds after opening it flatly claims the menu "has not been published" — even though the very link that opens it only appears when the menu does have a published version. "View all" (the sibling dialog, same underlying data) correctly shows "Loading history…" during the identical fetch; "Go back to…" has no equivalent branch.

Repro
  • Menu "QA timing c29341" — a real publish already in its history (confirmed via "View all").
  • Clicked go back to… (visible, because the menu has a published version).
  • Immediately: "Nothing to go back to yet — this menu has not been published."
  • ~5 seconds later, same dialog instance, no user action: "Sat 6:24am by QA Murphy — Go back to this."
  • Reproduced twice; confirmed via network trace that the correction lands the instant GET …/menus/{id}/history returns 200.
Expected
A loading indication (matching "View all"'s "Loading history…") while the fetch is in flight, only showing "nothing to go back to" once it's actually confirmed empty.
Actual
Claims "this menu has not been published" immediately on open, self-corrects a few seconds later once the fetch resolves.

Filed as #823. A regression case documenting this (expected red until fixed) is in PR #825.

Minor / cosmetic jmiedreich-ux/Vennusign#824

A publish shows up in the history changelog as a bare lowercase word

Every entry in "View all" and the sidebar history panel reads as a proper, capitalized sentence naming exactly what changed — except a publish, which renders as the raw, unstyled word published. Root cause: ContentRepository.PublishAsync always writes its history row with Detail = null, so the client falls back to the raw kind string. The system already computes a real summary of what shipped (shippedChanges) — it just never reaches this view.

Sections reordered              Page 1 · QA Murphy · Sat 6:24am
published                       QA Murphy · Sat 6:24am
Item added — Beta Item c29341   Page 1 · QA Murphy · Sat 6:24am
...

Nothing is functionally broken — filed as #824 because it sits in the same changelog "View all" is meant to make legible, and it's the one entry that reads like a debug string.

Environment observation

This venue is at its 50-menu ceiling — mostly from tonight's own testing — and everything was slow throughout

The QA venue went from 29 to exactly 50 menus over this session, almost entirely from throwaway test menus this run created. 50 is the venue's configured ceiling; hitting it correctly refuses with a clear, well-formed message ("That would be 51 menus, and this venue is set up for 50…") — that guardrail itself works. But it also means the venue has no room left, which is why PR #825's spec self-skipped on its first live run. Reported to #752 per standing instruction — not cleaned up.

Separately, and likely related: ordinary interactions — shelf load, adding an item, opening a history dialog, undo — regularly took 3–25 seconds throughout the night, slow enough that I twice mistook a working feature (undo/redo, canvas-to-inspector name sync) for broken before disproving it with a longer wait and a reload. Mid-session, #818 landed and deployed (build 8abcbdd9, after this run's testing window) — the owner's own real-browser timing found the exact same "fixed ~3–4s floor per action regardless of the action" shape and fixed part of its root cause (redundant/serial DB round trips in the back-office auth pipeline). A quick recheck against the new build after it deployed: adding a section now measures totalMs: 2964 (actionMs: 1513, refreshMs: 1451) — a real but modest improvement on the pre-fix baseline (~3.5–4s), consistent with #818's own caveat that this fix doesn't yet cover every round trip in the chain.
